reader_issues: Four unrelated modules (electrical-maths-module-1 to electrical-maths-module-4 covering Linear Algebra, ODEs, Laplace Transforms, and Fourier Series for Group B/Electrical) are bundled in the supplied notes alongside the Group A calculus notes (maths-module-1 to maths-module-4).

Editorial 'Note on the source' callouts appear in maths-module-1 (page 6), maths-module-2 (pages 10, 11), maths-module-3 (pages 3, 7, 9, 10, 12), and maths-module-4 (pages 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13) referencing errors in the original handwritten student notes.

In maths-module-4 (pages 12-13), the Method of Steepest Descent is presented using a fixed learning rate alpha rather than Kreyszig's Section 22.1 optimal step size t that minimizes g(t) = f(x - t grad f(x)) along the gradient direction.
uncertainties: Visual contents of external WebP images in maths-module-1 (pages 2, 18) and maths-module-4 (pages 6, 8) are not directly verifiable from text alone, though surrounding text substantively explains the concepts.

In maths-module-4, Steepest Descent uses fixed learning rates (0.1, 0.01) instead of Kreyszig's Cauchy line-search parameter t; it is uncertain whether KTU exams require the line-search formulation from Text 2 Section 22.1 or accept fixed-step gradient descent.

coverage.topic: Introduction: Relevance of technical drawing in engineering field (No questions for the end semester examination)
coverage.evidence: Page 1 ('Start here') briefly states 'Engineering drawing is how engineers describe a solid object on flat paper' via front and top views, but does not substantively discuss the broader relevance of technical drawing in the engineering field.
coverage.needed_fix: Add a brief overview explaining the relevance and role of technical drawing in engineering communication and manufacturing.

coverage.topic: Types of lines (No questions for the end semester examination)
coverage.evidence: Page 2 ('Drawing basics: lines and dimensions') covers continuous thick, continuous thin, dashed, and chain thin lines and their uses in a table.

coverage.topic: Dimensioning (No questions for the end semester examination)
coverage.evidence: Page 2 ('Drawing basics: lines and dimensions') explains dimension lines, extension lines, placement of numbers, and millimetre conventions.

coverage.topic: BIS code of practice for technical drawing (No questions for the end semester examination)
coverage.evidence: Page 2 mentions 'The BIS code of practice for technical drawing is not asked in the end-semester examination' in a callout, without explaining BIS standards (e.g., SP 46, sheet sizes, title blocks, scale conventions, or lettering standards).
coverage.needed_fix: Add a concise summary of BIS code of practice conventions for technical drawing.

coverage.topic: Projection of points in different quadrants
coverage.evidence: Page 3 ('Planes, quadrants and points') explains HP, VP, XY line, all four quadrants, first-angle projection, and works through an example projecting four points (A, B, C, D) across quadrants I–IV.

coverage.topic: Projection of straight lines inclined to one plane
coverage.evidence: Page 4 ('Positions of a line') lists lines parallel to both planes, perpendicular to HP/VP, and parallel to one plane and inclined to the other in a summary table with the rule that a line parallel to a plane shows true length on that plane, but provides no dedicated worked examples for lines inclined to only one plane before jumping to lines inclined to both planes.
coverage.needed_fix: Add 1–2 basic worked examples of straight lines parallel to one reference plane and inclined to the other.

coverage.topic: Projection of straight lines inclined to both planes
coverage.evidence: Pages 4 and 6–13 extensively cover lines inclined to both HP and VP using line rotation, reverse rotation, plane rotation (trapezoidal), midpoint, profile plane, and trace-based constructions.

coverage.topic: Trace of a line
coverage.evidence: Page 5 ('Traces of a line') defines Horizontal Trace (HT) and Vertical Trace (VT) and how to locate them; Pages 7–9 and 11–12 solve numerous problems finding traces and building projections from given traces.

coverage.topic: Inclination of lines with reference planes
coverage.evidence: Page 4 defines true inclinations (theta with HP, phi with VP) and apparent angles (alpha, beta), and Pages 7–13 calculate and construct them across varied problem types.

coverage.topic: True length and true inclinations of line inclined to both the reference planes
coverage.evidence: Pages 4 and 7–13 thoroughly explain and demonstrate finding true length (TL) and true inclinations (theta, phi) by both the Line Rotation Method and the Plane Rotation (Trapezoidal) Method.

coverage.topic: Projection of Simple solids (Triangular, Rectangle, Square, Pentagonal and Hexagonal Prisms, Pyramids, Cone and Cylinder only)
coverage.evidence: Pages 2–12 cover Triangular, Square, Pentagonal, and Hexagonal Prisms and Pyramids, Cones, Cylinders, and Cubes. However, Rectangular Prisms and Rectangular Pyramids are not explicitly demonstrated in Module 2.
coverage.needed_fix: Include explicit mention or an example involving a rectangular prism or rectangular pyramid in Module 2.

coverage.topic: Projection of solids in simple position including profile view
coverage.evidence: Page 2 ('Classification of Solids and the Simple Position') and Stage 1 of every worked problem cover simple position (axis perpendicular to HP or VP). However, constructing a profile view (side view on an auxiliary vertical/profile plane X1Y1) of a solid in simple position is not taught in Module 2 ('Profile Plane' in Module 2 Pages 5, 8, and 10 only refers to the axis or slant edge lying in a profile plane when theta + phi = 90 degrees, drawn in front and top views). Side view construction appears only in Module 3 Page 9 (Problem 93).
coverage.needed_fix: Add a section and worked example in Module 2 showing how to draw the profile (left/right side) view of a simple solid in simple position.

coverage.topic: Projection of solids with axis inclined to one of the reference planes
coverage.evidence: Pages 3, 4, and 6 explain and work through two-stage projections where the solid is inclined to one reference plane (HP or VP) and parallel to the other (e.g., Page 4 worked example of a cone on HP with axis parallel to VP; Page 6 worked example of a freely suspended square pyramid with axis parallel to VP; plus Stage 2 of all three-stage problems).

coverage.topic: Projection of solids with axis inclined to both reference planes
coverage.evidence: Pages 3–12 extensively cover three-stage projections of solids inclined to both HP and VP, including direct Stage-3 rotation, resting on faces/slant edges/generators, locus method for apparent angle beta, complementary profile-plane cases, solids resting on VP, and freely suspended solids.

coverage.topic: Sections of Solids: Sections of Prisms, Pyramids, Cone and Cylinder only, with axis in vertical position and cut by different section planes (Exclude true shape given problems)
coverage.evidence: Pages 2–4 and 7–9 cover sections of vertical prisms, pyramids, cylinders, and cones cut by horizontal, auxiliary inclined (AIP), auxiliary vertical (AVP), and profile cutting planes, and Page 4 explicitly notes the exclusion of reverse true-shape-given problems.

coverage.topic: True shape of the sections (Exclude true shape given problems)
coverage.evidence: Pages 3, 4, and 7–9 explain and construct the true shape of sections using auxiliary reference lines (x1-y1) parallel to the cutting plane trace as well as direct front/side view true shapes for planes parallel to VP or profile planes.

coverage.topic: Development of Surfaces: Development of surfaces of the solids (Exclude problems with through holes)
coverage.evidence: Pages 5, 6, 10, and 11 explain and construct full lateral surface developments of intact prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones, and frustums using parallel-line and radial-line methods (including shortest-path/helix applications on intact solids in Problems 131, 136, 145, 150, 152, 153), with no through-hole development problems.

coverage.topic: Development of surfaces of solids cut by different section planes (Exclude problems with through holes)
coverage.evidence: Pages 5, 6, 10, and 11 demonstrate lateral surface developments of truncated square, pentagonal, and hexagonal prisms, truncated cylinders (including compound/mitre cuts), and truncated square/pentagonal pyramids and cones cut by single or multiple section planes.

coverage.topic: Isometric Projection: Isometric scale
coverage.evidence: Page 2 ('Isometric Axes, Planes, and the Isometric Scale') explains the foreshortening ratio (cos 30 / cos 45 ≈ 0.8165), contrasts isometric projection with isometric view, and provides a step-by-step worked example constructing a graphical isometric scale.

coverage.topic: Isometric View and Projections of Prisms, Pyramids, Cone, Cylinder, Sphere, Hemisphere
coverage.evidence: Pages 2–6 explain and demonstrate isometric views and projections of individual cubes, hexagonal and pentagonal prisms, pyramids, frustums, cylinders, cones, hemispheres, and spheres using the box/offset method, four-center ellipse method, and true-radius sphere rule.

coverage.topic: Isometric View and Projections of combinations of Prisms, Pyramids, Cone, Cylinder, Sphere, Hemisphere
coverage.evidence: Pages 5–9 extensively cover coaxial and stacked combinations of slabs, cubes, prisms, pyramids, frustums, cylinders, cones, hemispheres, and spheres.

coverage.topic: Computer Aided Drawing (CAD): Introduction, Role of CAD in design and development of new products (CAD, only internal evaluation)
coverage.evidence: Page 10 ('Computer Aided Drawing (CAD)') introduces CAD and explains its role in product development, design iteration, component reuse, and manufacturing communication.

coverage.topic: Advantages of CAD (CAD, only internal evaluation)
coverage.evidence: Page 10 ('Advantages of CAD') lists and explains accuracy, efficient revision, reuse, clear communication, and storage/exchange.

coverage.topic: Creating two-dimensional drawing with dimensions using suitable software (CAD, only internal evaluation)
coverage.evidence: Page 10 ('Creating a dimensioned two-dimensional drawing' and 'Example command sequence and practice task') outlines a 6-step 2D CAD workflow, typical commands (LINE, CIRCLE, OFFSET, TRIM, LAYER, dimension tools), and a practice exercise.

module_boundary_issues.topic: Projection of solids in simple position including profile view
module_boundary_issues.needed_fix: Profile (side) view construction using a vertical reference line x'y' and 45-degree mitre line / compass arcs is only demonstrated in Module 3 Page 9 (Problem 93: Hexagonal pyramid cut by a profile plane), whereas the syllabus places 'Projection of solids in simple position including profile view' in Module 2. Add profile view construction for simple solids in simple position to Module 2.

coverage.official_module: Module 1: Electrochemistry and Corrosion Science (9 Hours)
coverage.topic: Electrode potential
coverage.evidence: Covers origin of single electrode potential, Helmholtz electrical double layer, standard electrode potential, and IUPAC reduction convention.

coverage.official_module: Module 1: Electrochemistry and Corrosion Science (9 Hours)
coverage.topic: Nernst equation for single electrode and cell (Numerical problems)
coverage.evidence: Derives Nernst equation from van 't Hoff isotherm for single electrodes and complete cells; chemistry-module-1 provides 15 worked numerical problems and chemistry-ece-module-1 provides 7.
coverage.needed_fix: In chemistry-ece-module-1 (page 4), add complete cell EMF numerical problems with non-unit ion concentrations (currently only single-electrode, ΔG, and K problems are solved there, though chemistry-module-1 covers all types).

coverage.official_module: Module 1: Electrochemistry and Corrosion Science (9 Hours)
coverage.topic: Reference electrodes - SHE & Calomel electrode - Construction and Working
coverage.evidence: Details primary (SHE) and secondary (Calomel/SCE) reference electrodes, including construction, cell representations, anode/cathode half-reactions, Nernst equations, and limitations.

coverage.official_module: Module 1: Electrochemistry and Corrosion Science (9 Hours)
coverage.topic: Electrochemical series - Applications
coverage.evidence: Defines the electrochemical series and explains applications: standard cell EMF calculation, relative ease of oxidation/reduction, metal and hydrogen displacement, redox spontaneity, and electrolysis product prediction.

coverage.official_module: Module 1: Electrochemistry and Corrosion Science (9 Hours)
coverage.topic: Glass Electrode & pH Measurement
coverage.evidence: Explains glass bulb composition, internal reference, ion-exchange membrane potential, coupling with SCE for potentiometric pH measurement, calibration, advantages, and limitations.

coverage.official_module: Module 1: Electrochemistry and Corrosion Science (9 Hours)
coverage.topic: Conductivity - Measurement using Digital conductivity meter
coverage.evidence: Defines conductance, specific conductivity, cell constant, calibration with 0.1 M KCl, measurement procedure with a digital conductivity meter, and worked numericals.

coverage.official_module: Module 1: Electrochemistry and Corrosion Science (9 Hours)
coverage.topic: Li-ion battery construction and working
coverage.evidence: Covers lithiated graphite anode, LiCoO2 cathode, organic carbonate electrolyte, separator, and intercalation/de-intercalation reactions during charging and discharging.

coverage.official_module: Module 1: Electrochemistry and Corrosion Science (9 Hours)
coverage.topic: H2-O2 fuel cell (acid electrolyte only) construction and working
coverage.evidence: chemistry-module-1 (page 9) covers the phosphoric acid (H3PO4) H2-O2 fuel cell with proton-transfer reactions. However, chemistry-ece-module-1 (page 7) only describes the alkaline (25% KOH/NaOH) H2-O2 fuel cell.
coverage.needed_fix: Replace the alkaline (KOH/NaOH) H2-O2 fuel cell in chemistry-ece-module-1 (page 7) with the acid-electrolyte H2-O2 fuel cell required by the syllabus (as already present in chemistry-module-1 page 9).

coverage.official_module: Module 1: Electrochemistry and Corrosion Science (9 Hours)
coverage.topic: Corrosion - Electrochemical corrosion mechanism (acidic & alkaline medium)
coverage.evidence: Explains dry vs wet corrosion, hydrogen evolution mechanism in acidic and alkaline media, oxygen absorption mechanism in acidic and neutral/alkaline media, rusting of iron, and differential aeration.

coverage.official_module: Module 1: Electrochemistry and Corrosion Science (9 Hours)
coverage.topic: Galvanic series
coverage.evidence: Defines the galvanic series in seawater, role of passivity, comparison table against the electrochemical series, and galvanic corrosion prediction.

coverage.official_module: Module 1: Electrochemistry and Corrosion Science (9 Hours)
coverage.topic: Corrosion control methods - Cathodic Protection - Sacrificial anodic protection and impressed current cathodic protection
coverage.evidence: Details sacrificial anode protection (Mg, Zn, Al) and impressed current cathodic protection (ICCP) with DC source and insoluble anode, including mechanisms, pros/cons, and applications.

coverage.official_module: Module 1: Electrochemistry and Corrosion Science (9 Hours)
coverage.topic: Electroplating of copper
coverage.evidence: Covers surface pretreatment, CuSO4 bath setup, cathode/anode reactions, soluble vs inert anodes, and applications.

coverage.official_module: Module 1: Electrochemistry and Corrosion Science (9 Hours)
coverage.topic: Electroless plating of copper
coverage.evidence: Covers autocatalytic deposition principle, SnCl2/PdCl2 activation, alkaline CuSO4-HCHO-EDTA bath composition, half-reactions, overall reaction, and PCB through-hole applications.
coverage.needed_fix: Fix the typo in chemistry-ece-module-1 (page 9) where the 'Overall reaction' under Electroless Plating of Copper is erroneously written for Nickel hypophosphite (Ni2+ + H2PO2- + H2O -> Ni + H2PO3- + 2H+) instead of Copper formaldehyde.

coverage.official_module: Module 2: Materials for Electronic Applications (9 Hrs)
coverage.topic: Nanomaterials - Classification based on Dimension & Materials
coverage.evidence: Classifies nanomaterials into 0D, 1D, 2D, and 3D and by material composition (carbon-based, metal/oxide/semiconductor, nanocomposites, dendrimers, biological).

coverage.official_module: Module 2: Materials for Electronic Applications (9 Hrs)
coverage.topic: Nanomaterials - Synthesis - Sol gel & Chemical Reduction
coverage.evidence: Explains top-down vs bottom-up approaches, chemical reduction (AgNO3 with trisodium citrate, MoCl2 reduction), and alkoxide hydrolysis/sol-gel synthesis (SiO2, TiO2, Al2O3, xerogel vs aerogel).

coverage.official_module: Module 2: Materials for Electronic Applications (9 Hrs)
coverage.topic: Applications of nanomaterials
coverage.evidence: chemistry-module-2 (page 6) substantively covers applications in catalysis, gas sensors, electronics/optoelectronics, coatings/tyres, environmental remediation, and biomedicine; chemistry-ece-module-2 (page 2) gives a brief summary.

coverage.official_module: Module 2: Materials for Electronic Applications (9 Hrs)
coverage.topic: Carbon Nanotubes - structure, properties & application
coverage.evidence: Covers SWCNT (armchair, zigzag, chiral) and MWCNT (Russian doll, parchment, mixed) structures, chirality rules, electrical/thermal/mechanical properties, and applications.

coverage.official_module: Module 2: Materials for Electronic Applications (9 Hrs)
coverage.topic: Fullerenes - structure, properties & application
coverage.evidence: Covers truncated icosahedral C60 cage structure (12 pentagons, 20 hexagons, [6,6] and [5,6] bonds), synthesis, physical/chemical/electrical properties, and applications.

coverage.official_module: Module 2: Materials for Electronic Applications (9 Hrs)
coverage.topic: Graphene - structure, properties & application
coverage.evidence: Covers 2D sp2 honeycomb lattice, Dirac points, synthesis routes, mechanical/electrical/thermal/optical properties, and applications.

coverage.official_module: Module 2: Materials for Electronic Applications (9 Hrs)
coverage.topic: Carbon Quantum Dots - structure, properties & application
coverage.evidence: Explains <10 nm quasi-spherical carbon structure, surface functional groups, top-down/bottom-up synthesis, optical/luminescence and biocompatibility properties, and applications.
coverage.needed_fix: In chemistry-ece-module-2 (page 4), expand the Applications of CQDs beyond the single biomedical bullet to match the broader applications in sensing, catalysis, and optoelectronics.

coverage.official_module: Module 2: Materials for Electronic Applications (9 Hrs)
coverage.topic: Polymers - Fire Retardant Polymers - Halogenated & Non-halogenated polymers (Examples only)
coverage.evidence: Covers polymer basics, non-halogenated fire-retardant polymers (novolac, bakelite, polyimides, polybenzoxazoles, silicones), and halogenated examples (PVC, neoprene, polybromostyrene, brominated butyl rubber, PBDE/PCDE) with radical-quenching mechanisms.

coverage.official_module: Module 2: Materials for Electronic Applications (9 Hrs)
coverage.topic: Conducting Polymers - Classification
coverage.evidence: Classifies conducting polymers into Intrinsically Conducting Polymers (conjugated pi-backbone and p-/n-/protonic-doped) and Extrinsically Conducting Polymers (conductive-element-filled and blended).

coverage.official_module: Module 2: Materials for Electronic Applications (9 Hrs)
coverage.topic: Polyaniline & Polypyrrole - synthesis, properties and applications
coverage.evidence: Covers chemical and electrochemical oxidative polymerization, oxidation/protonation states (emeraldine salt/base), properties, and applications for both Polyaniline and Polypyrrole.

coverage.official_module: Module 2: Materials for Electronic Applications (9 Hrs)
coverage.topic: Organic electronic materials and devices - construction, working and applications of Organic Light Emitting Diode (OLED)
coverage.evidence: Details the multilayer OLED stack (substrate, ITO anode, HTL, EML/ETL, metal cathode), charge injection, exciton formation, LUMO-to-HOMO radiative recombination, pros/cons, and display applications.

coverage.official_module: Module 2: Materials for Electronic Applications (9 Hrs)
coverage.topic: Organic electronic materials and devices - construction, working and applications of Dye-Sensitized Solar Cells (DSSC)
coverage.evidence: Details DSSC components (TCO substrate, mesoporous TiO2, ruthenium/organic dye photosensitizer, I-/I3- electrolyte, Pt/graphite counter electrode), four-step photoelectrochemical charge cycle, advantages, and applications.

coverage.official_module: Module 2: Materials for Electronic Applications (9 Hrs)
coverage.topic: Materials used in Quantum computing Technology
coverage.evidence: Explains qubits, superposition, entanglement, interference, decoherence, and qubit materials including superconducting metals (Al, Nb, TiN), h-BN, diamond NV centers, isotopically purified 28Si, nanowires, and InAs/GaAs quantum dots.

coverage.official_module: Module 2: Materials for Electronic Applications (9 Hrs)
coverage.topic: Super capacitors
coverage.evidence: Explains EDLC/pseudocapacitor mechanisms, components (porous carbon/nanomaterial electrodes, electrolytes, separator, current collectors, PVDF/PAN binders), energy equations, battery vs capacitor comparison, pros/cons, and applications.

coverage.official_module: Module 2: Materials for Electronic Applications (9 Hrs)
coverage.topic: Spintronics
coverage.evidence: Explains electron spin polarization, Giant Magnetoresistance (GMR), Tunnel Magnetoresistance (TMR), metal/insulator stacks (CoFeB, MgO, Al2O3), diluted magnetic semiconductors (InAs/GaAs with Mn), graphene spin channels, and MRAM/HDD applications.

coverage.official_module: Module 3: Molecular Spectroscopy and Analytical Techniques (9 Hours)
coverage.topic: Spectroscopy - Types of spectra
coverage.evidence: Covers electromagnetic radiation, absorption vs emission vs scattering processes, and atomic (line) vs molecular (band) spectra.

coverage.official_module: Module 3: Molecular Spectroscopy and Analytical Techniques (9 Hours)
coverage.topic: Molecular energy levels
coverage.evidence: Explains electronic, vibrational, rotational, and translational energy levels, the Born-Oppenheimer approximation, and the hierarchy ΔE_ele > ΔE_vib > ΔE_rot >> ΔE_trans.

coverage.official_module: Module 3: Molecular Spectroscopy and Analytical Techniques (9 Hours)
coverage.topic: Beer Lambert's law - Numerical problems
coverage.evidence: Derives A = εcl from differential attenuation, discusses transmittance, absorbance, units of ε, deviations, and provides multiple solved numerical problems in both note sets.

coverage.official_module: Module 3: Molecular Spectroscopy and Analytical Techniques (9 Hours)
coverage.topic: Electronic Spectroscopy - Principle, Types of electronic transitions
coverage.evidence: Explains UV-Vis absorption principle, σ→σ*, n→σ*, π→π*, and n→π* transitions, relative energy ordering, chromophores, auxochromes, and spectral shifts.

coverage.official_module: Module 3: Molecular Spectroscopy and Analytical Techniques (9 Hours)
coverage.topic: Role of conjugation in absorption maxima
coverage.evidence: Explains how extended π-conjugation narrows the HOMO-LUMO gap and causes bathochromic shifts in λ_max across ethene (169 nm), 1,3-butadiene (217 nm), 1,3,5-hexatriene (247-250 nm), and lycopene (505 nm).

coverage.official_module: Module 3: Molecular Spectroscopy and Analytical Techniques (9 Hours)
coverage.topic: Electronic Spectroscopy - Instrumentation and Applications
coverage.evidence: Details double-beam UV-Vis spectrophotometer components (radiation sources, monochromator, beam splitter, quartz cuvettes, detectors), optical path, reference blank, and analytical applications.

coverage.official_module: Module 3: Molecular Spectroscopy and Analytical Techniques (9 Hours)
coverage.topic: Vibrational spectroscopy - Principle
coverage.evidence: Explains quantized vibrational transitions, dipole-moment change selection rule (∂μ/∂Q ≠ 0), stretching (symmetric, asymmetric) and bending (scissoring, rocking, wagging, twisting) vibrations, and Hooke's law / harmonic oscillator force constant calculations.

coverage.official_module: Module 3: Molecular Spectroscopy and Analytical Techniques (9 Hours)
coverage.topic: Number of vibrational modes - Vibrational modes of CO2 and H2O
coverage.evidence: Derives 3N-5 (linear) and 3N-6 (non-linear) mode formulas, and analyzes the 4 modes of CO2 (symmetric stretch inactive, asymmetric stretch active, 2 degenerate bends active) and 3 active modes of bent H2O.

coverage.official_module: Module 3: Molecular Spectroscopy and Analytical Techniques (9 Hours)
coverage.topic: Vibrational spectroscopy - Applications
coverage.evidence: Covers functional group and fingerprint region identification, force constant determination, purity testing, reaction kinetics, and distinguishing intra- vs intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

coverage.official_module: Module 3: Molecular Spectroscopy and Analytical Techniques (9 Hours)
coverage.topic: Thermal Analysis: Dielectric Thermal Analysis (DETA) of Polymers - Working and Application
coverage.evidence: Covers dipolar relaxation and ionic migration under an AC field, storage permittivity (ε'), dielectric loss (ε''), loss tangent (tan δ), DETA furnace/electrode instrumentation, working, and applications in polymer Tg and curing.

coverage.official_module: Module 3: Molecular Spectroscopy and Analytical Techniques (9 Hours)
coverage.topic: Electron Microscopic Techniques: SEM - Principle, instrumentation and Applications
coverage.evidence: Explains electron-sample interactions (SE, BSE, characteristic X-rays), SEM column components (electron gun, anode, condenser/objective lenses, scan coils, vacuum chamber, detectors), working, conductive sample coating, and applications.

coverage.topic: Water characteristics - Hardness - Types of hardness - Temporary and Permanent
coverage.evidence: Defines hard and soft water, soap scum precipitation reactions with sodium stearate, temporary (carbonate/bicarbonate) hardness and its thermal removal, and permanent (non-carbonate) hardness.

coverage.topic: Disadvantages of hard water
coverage.evidence: Explains domestic soap wastage and industrial disadvantages including boiler scale and sludge formation, priming and foaming, boiler corrosion (MgCl2 hydrolysis), and dyeing/sugar processing issues.

coverage.topic: Degree of hardness (Numericals)
coverage.evidence: Explains CaCO3 equivalence, equivalent masses, hardness units (mg/L, ppm, meq/L, °Fr, °Cl), alkalinity vs hardness partitioning, and provides 11 worked numerical examples in chemistry-module-4 and 4 in chemistry-ece-module-4.

coverage.topic: Water softening methods - Ion exchange process - Principle, procedure and advantages
coverage.evidence: Covers cation (RH) and anion (R'OH) exchange resins, two-column demineralization reactions, column sequencing rationale, acid/alkali regeneration equations, advantages, and limitations.

coverage.topic: Reverse osmosis - principle, process and advantages
coverage.evidence: Explains natural osmosis vs reverse osmosis (ΔP > Δπ), semipermeable membranes (cellulose acetate, aromatic polyamide), desalination process steps, advantages, and comparison with ion exchange.

coverage.topic: Water disinfection methods - chlorination - Break point chlorination, ozone and UV irradiation
coverage.evidence: Details chlorination (Cl2, chloramine, bleaching powder/hypochlorites, HOCl/OCl- pH dependence), the four stages of the breakpoint chlorination curve, dechlorination, ozonation, and UV-C irradiation.

coverage.topic: Dissolved oxygen (DO), BOD and COD - Definition & Significance
coverage.evidence: Defines DO, BOD5 (5 days at 20 °C in dark, with worked dilution example in chemistry-module-4), and COD (acidified K2Cr2O7 reflux), along with factors affecting DO and environmental significance.

coverage.topic: Waste Management: Sewage water treatment - Primary, Secondary and Tertiary - Flow diagram
coverage.evidence: Provides process flow diagrams and explains preliminary/primary (screening, grit removal, sedimentation), secondary biological (activated sludge, trickling filter, UASB), and tertiary (phosphate precipitation with lime, nitrogen stripping/denitrification, chlorination) stages.

coverage.topic: Trickling filter and UASB process
coverage.evidence: Details aerobic attached-growth trickling filter construction/working and anaerobic Upflow Anaerobic Sludge Blanket (UASB) reactor construction/working, biogas collection, and comparison.

coverage.topic: E Waste, Methods of disposal - recycle, recovery and reuse
coverage.evidence: chemistry-module-4 (page 11) thoroughly covers e-waste composition, toxic hazards (Pb, Cd, Hg, Be), and the 4R hierarchy (Reduce, Reuse, Recycle, Recover). However, this topic is completely missing from chemistry-ece-module-4.
coverage.needed_fix: Add E-waste and methods of disposal (recycle, recovery, and reuse) to chemistry-ece-module-4 (or unify notes onto chemistry-module-4).

coverage.topic: Chemistry of climate change - Greenhouse Gases
coverage.evidence: chemistry-module-4 (page 12) covers the greenhouse effect mechanism, IR-active vibrational modes of GHGs (CO2, H2O, CH4, N2O, CFCs), natural vs enhanced greenhouse effect, anthropogenic sources, and mitigation/adaptation. Missing from chemistry-ece-module-4.
coverage.needed_fix: Add Chemistry of climate change and Greenhouse Gases to chemistry-ece-module-4 (or unify notes onto chemistry-module-4).

coverage.topic: Ozone Depletion
coverage.evidence: chemistry-module-4 (page 13) covers stratospheric ozone, the Chapman cycle, catalytic free-radical ozone destruction by CFCs (Cl•) and NOx, biological impacts, and the Montreal Protocol. Missing from chemistry-ece-module-4.
coverage.needed_fix: Add Ozone Depletion to chemistry-ece-module-4 (or unify notes onto chemistry-module-4).

coverage.topic: Sustainable Development - an introduction to Sustainable Development Goals
coverage.evidence: chemistry-module-4 (page 14) covers the Brundtland definition, the three pillars of sustainability (environmental, social, economic), all 17 UN SDGs, alignment with environmental chemistry, and engineering trade-offs. Missing from chemistry-ece-module-4.
coverage.needed_fix: Add Sustainable Development and the 17 SDGs to chemistry-ece-module-4 (or unify notes onto chemistry-module-4).

reader_issues: Duplicate module sets exist in the repository: 'chemistry-ece-module-1..4' and 'chemistry-module-1..4'. 'chemistry-module-1..4' is complete, rigorous, and fully aligned with GXCYT122, whereas 'chemistry-ece-module-1..4' has several gaps and errors.

In chemistry-ece-module-1 (page 7), the H2-O2 fuel cell is taught using an alkaline electrolyte (25% KOH or NaOH), violating the official syllabus specification 'H2-O2 fuel cell (acid electrolyte only)'. (chemistry-module-1 page 9 correctly teaches the acidic H3PO4 fuel cell).

In chemistry-ece-module-1 (page 9), under 'Electroless Plating of Copper', the 'Overall reaction' is erroneously given for nickel plating with hypophosphite (Ni2+ + H2PO2- + H2O -> Ni + H2PO3- + 2H+) instead of copper plating with formaldehyde.

In chemistry-ece-module-1 (page 4), the Nernst equation section lacks solved numerical problems for complete electrochemical cells at non-standard concentrations (only single-electrode potentials, ΔG, and equilibrium constant K are solved there).
In chemistry-ece-module-1 (page 7) and chemistry-ece-module-2 (page 5), percent signs are dropped in several places (e.g., 'up to 90 (x=0.9)', '40 > Ni-Cd', '25 KOH', 'efficient (75 )').
In chemistry-ece-module-3 (page 7), there is a LaTeX typo in dielectric loss: (\'\varepsilon\'\').

In chemistry-ece-module-4, the final four syllabus topics of Module 4 (E-Waste disposal/recycle/recovery/reuse, Chemistry of climate change & Greenhouse Gases, Ozone Depletion, and Sustainable Development & SDGs) are completely omitted, although they are thoroughly covered in chemistry-module-4 (pages 11-14).

coverage.topic: Modularization and Motivation for modularization
coverage.evidence: Page 7 defines modular design and explains its motivation (reducing duplicated logic, hiding implementation detail, reuse, debugging, testing).

coverage.topic: Functions with multiple return values

coverage.topic: Reasons for using Recursion
coverage.evidence: Page 30 ('Why use recursion?') explains when and why recursion is useful and its trade-offs.

coverage.topic: The Call Stack and Recursion and the Stack
coverage.evidence: Page 31 explains the call stack, stack frames, push/pop order, and traces factorial(3).

coverage.topic: Avoiding Circularity in Recursion
coverage.evidence: Page 31 ('Avoid circularity') explains base cases, progress toward the base case, and how circular calls lead to RecursionError.

coverage.topic: Recursion sample problem: Finding the nth Fibonacci number
coverage.evidence: Page 31 provides the recursive fibonacci(n) implementation and recurrence relation.

coverage.topic: Recursion sample problem: greatest common divisor of two positive integers
coverage.evidence: Page 31 provides the recursive gcd(a, b) implementation using Euclid's algorithm.

coverage.topic: Recursion sample problem: the factorial of a positive integer
coverage.evidence: Page 31 provides the recursive factorial(n) implementation and stack trace.

coverage.topic: Recursion sample problem: adding two positive integers
coverage.evidence: Page 31 provides the recursive add(a, b) implementation.

coverage.topic: Recursion sample problem: the sum of digits of a positive number
coverage.evidence: Page 31 provides the recursive sum_digits(n) implementation.

coverage.topic: Brute-force Approach (Example: Padlock, Password guessing)
coverage.evidence: Page 3 explains the brute-force approach and demonstrates both the 4-digit padlock combination example and the password-guessing search space example.

coverage.topic: Divide-and-conquer Approach (Example: The Merge Sort Algorithm)
coverage.evidence: Page 4 explains divide, conquer, and combine steps and demonstrates Merge Sort with diagram and Python implementation.

coverage.topic: Advantages of Divide and Conquer Approach
coverage.evidence: Page 4 lists five advantages of Divide and Conquer (simplifies problems, efficiency, cache usage, numerical accuracy, parallel execution).

coverage.topic: Disadvantages of Divide and Conquer Approach
coverage.evidence: Page 4 lists three disadvantages of Divide and Conquer (recursion overhead, complexity for large inputs, overkill for simple tasks).

coverage.topic: Dynamic Programming Approach (Example: Fibonacci series)
coverage.evidence: Page 5 explains overlapping sub-problems, memoization, and bottom-up tabulation using the Fibonacci series example.

coverage.topic: Recursion vs Dynamic Programming
coverage.evidence: Page 5 ('Recursion versus dynamic programming') contrasts plain recursion/divide-and-conquer with dynamic programming on overlapping sub-problems.

coverage.topic: Greedy Algorithm Approach (Example: maximum number of tasks completed in limited time)
coverage.evidence: Page 6 explains the Greedy approach and includes both activity selection and the exact syllabus example of maximizing the number of tasks completed in a limited amount of time.

coverage.topic: Motivations for the Greedy Approach
coverage.evidence: Page 6 ('Why use greedy?') explains the motivations for greedy algorithms (immediate feasible solution without backtracking, single-pass reduction).

coverage.topic: Characteristics of the Greedy Algorithm
coverage.evidence: Page 6 ('Characteristics') lists the characteristics of greedy algorithms (ordered list of resources with costs/constraints, taking maximum resource allowed at each step).

coverage.topic: Greedy Algorithms vs Dynamic Programming
coverage.evidence: Page 6 provides a comparison table between Greedy and Dynamic Programming across decision method, look-back, optimality, and cost.

coverage.topic: Randomized Approach - Example 1: Coupon collector (jeans coupons)
coverage.evidence: Page 7 ('Example 1: coupon collector') explains the jeans coupon collector problem with simulation code, steps, and expected value formula.

coverage.topic: Randomized Approach - Example 2: Hat-check problem
coverage.evidence: Page 7 ('Example 2: hat check') explains the party hat-check problem with simulation code, steps, and expected value of 1.

coverage.topic: Motivations for the Randomized Approach
coverage.evidence: Page 7 ('Motivation') lists simplicity, large problem spaces, fairness, robustness, and mathematical guarantees.

reader_issues: In python-module-1 (pages 1 through 12), almost every page contains duplicated content where the entire second half of the page repeats the first half verbatim or near-verbatim as a 'Review' or 'Reference' section.
In python-module-1 page 4, the percentage conversion formula in the review section is misprinted as 'Average (in percentage) = (Average_2 / 13)' instead of '(Average_2 / 12) * 100'.

In python-module-1 page 4, the binary machine code formula in the review section mis aligns the underbraces: '1010' has no label, '0011' is labeled 'add', '0110' is labeled '3', and an empty space is labeled '6'.

In python-module-1 page 7, the explicit type conversion code comments do not match the code: `y = int("15"); print(y + 5)` has comment `# Output: 15`, and `z = float(y); print(z)` has comment `# Output: 10.0` instead of `20` and `15.0`.
In python-module-1 page 10, the Assignment Operators output shows `a += 5 : 105` (and subsequent values `100`, `500`, `100.0`) when `a` was initialized to `10` (`10 + 5` should be `15`).
In python-module-1 page 11, the Bitwise Operators output prints `a >> 2 : 240` for left shift instead of `a << 2 : 240`.
In python-module-1 page 11, stray text 'College' appears at the end of the Operator Precedence section, and stray page numbers ('46' on page 9, '53' on page 12) remain in the text.
In python-module-1 page 12, C-style operators (`&&`, `||`) are used in the expression evaluation table (`C&&D`, `A+3 < B*1 || C&&D`) instead of Python's `and` and `or`.
In python-module-2, HTML page comments have non-sequential numbering from page 14 onward (jumping from page 14 to 15-27, then repeating 26 and 27 multiple times).

coverage.topic: Intrinsic semiconductor
coverage.evidence: Page 3 defines intrinsic semiconductors (e.g., Si, Ge) and lists six key properties including equal carrier concentrations (n = p) and temperature dependence.

coverage.topic: Derivation of density of electrons in conduction band
coverage.evidence: Page 3 provides the complete step-by-step integral derivation of n = N_c e^{(E_F - E_c)/kT} using conduction-band density of states Z(E) and Fermi-Dirac distribution F(E).

coverage.topic: Derivation of density of holes in valence band
coverage.evidence: Page 3 includes 'Derivation of hole concentration in the valence band', integrating Z_v(E)[1 - F(E)] from -infinity to E_v to obtain p = N_v e^{-(E_F - E_v)/kT}.

coverage.topic: Intrinsic carrier concentration
coverage.evidence: Page 4 derives n_i = (N_c N_v)^{1/2} e^{-E_g / 2kT} = 2 (2 pi k T / h^2)^{3/2} (m_e* m_h*)^{3/4} e^{-E_g / 2kT} from n_i^2 = n p.

coverage.topic: Variation of Intrinsic carrier concentration with temperature
coverage.evidence: Page 4 has a dedicated section 'Variation of Intrinsic Carrier Concentration with Temperature' explaining exponential growth with T, band-gap threshold effects, and device leakage.

coverage.topic: Extrinsic semiconductor (qualitative)
coverage.evidence: Page 5 covers doping, n-type (pentavalent donors) and p-type (trivalent acceptors) semiconductors, majority/minority carriers, and comparison tables.

coverage.topic: Formation of p-n junction
coverage.evidence: Page 6 explains joining p-type and n-type semiconductors, carrier diffusion, electron-hole recombination, immobile donor/acceptor ions, depletion region, and built-in potential V_0.

coverage.topic: Fermi level in semiconductors-intrinsic and extrinsic
coverage.evidence: Page 4 defines Fermi level and derives E_F = (E_v + E_c)/2 for intrinsic semiconductors; Page 5 describes and illustrates the shift of E_F toward E_C in n-type and toward E_V in p-type extrinsic semiconductors.

coverage.topic: Energy band diagram of p-n junction
coverage.evidence: Page 6 explains and plots JSXGraph energy band diagrams of a p-n junction under equilibrium (barrier qV_0), forward bias (barrier q(V_0 - V)), and reverse bias (barrier q(V_0 + V_R)).

coverage.topic: Qualitative description of charge flow across a p-n junction
coverage.evidence: Page 6 describes majority-carrier diffusion across the concentration gradient, minority-carrier drift due to the internal electric field, and equilibrium balance of drift and diffusion currents.

coverage.topic: Forward and reverse biased p-n junctions
coverage.evidence: Pages 6 and 7 explain barrier height and depletion width changes, majority carrier injection in forward bias, and minority carrier saturation current and breakdown in reverse bias.

coverage.topic: Diode equation (Derivation)
coverage.evidence: Page 7 derives I = I_0 (e^{V/V_T} - 1) and the practical form I = I_0 (e^{V/(eta V_T)} - 1) using Boltzmann carrier relations.

coverage.topic: V-I Characteristics of p-n junction
coverage.evidence: Page 7 provides the V-I measurement circuit, schematic V-I curve, description of zero, forward, and reverse bias regions, and definitions of knee voltage, reverse saturation current, and PIV.

coverage.topic: Semiconductor devices - Rectifiers - Half wave
coverage.evidence: Page 2 explains half-wave rectifier circuit, positive/negative half-cycle operation, input/output waveforms, PIV, disadvantages, and derives efficiency (max 40.6%); Page 3 gives ripple factor (1.21).

coverage.topic: Semiconductor devices - Rectifiers - Full wave
coverage.evidence: Page 3 covers both centre-tap and bridge full-wave rectifiers, working principles, PIV, pros/cons, efficiency derivation (max 81.2%), and ripple factor (0.48).

coverage.topic: Zener diode - V-I characteristics
coverage.evidence: Page 4 covers Zener diode construction, circuit symbol, forward/reverse operation, and plots and explains the I-V characteristic curve in the first and third quadrants.

coverage.topic: Zener breakdown and Avalanche breakdown
coverage.evidence: Page 4 explains the high-field bond-breaking mechanism of Zener breakdown and provides an 8-point comparison table contrasting Zener breakdown and Avalanche breakdown.

coverage.topic: Tunnel diode - V-I characteristics
coverage.evidence: Page 5 explains heavy doping and quantum tunneling, shows the symbol and I-V curve, and details the forward tunneling region (up to I_p, V_p), negative resistance region (to I_v, V_v), and normal diffusion region.

coverage.topic: Applications of Zener and Tunnel diodes
coverage.evidence: Page 4 lists Zener diode applications (voltage regulator, over-voltage protection, clipping/clamping); Page 5 lists Tunnel diode applications (ultra-high-speed switches, oscillators, logic memory storage, satellite microwave circuits).

coverage.topic: Photonic devices (qualitative) - Photo detectors (Junction and PIN photodiodes)
coverage.evidence: Page 6 introduces photonics and photodetectors, then explains the construction, reverse-bias operation, dark current, and photocurrent of junction photodiodes and the intrinsic-layer structure and advantages of PIN photodiodes.

coverage.topic: Applications of Photo detectors
coverage.evidence: Page 6 includes a section 'Applications of junction and PIN photodiodes' covering optical communication receivers, light meters, smoke detectors, barcode scanners/encoders, and medical/industrial instruments.

coverage.topic: Solar cells - V-I Characteristics
coverage.evidence: Page 7 explains the photovoltaic principle, solar cell construction, I-V and P-V curves, short-circuit current (I_sc), open-circuit voltage (V_oc), and maximum power point (P_max).

coverage.topic: Solar cells - Efficiency
coverage.evidence: Page 7 defines and gives formulas for conversion efficiency (eta = P_max / (light intensity * area)) and Fill Factor (f = P_max / (V_oc * I_sc)).

coverage.topic: Stringing of Solar cells to solar panel
coverage.evidence: Page 7 explains series stringing (V_oc(total) = N * V_oc, I_sc constant) and parallel stringing (I_sc(total) = N * I_sc, V_oc constant) with tables and JSXGraph I-V curves.

coverage.topic: Light Emitting Diode
coverage.evidence: Page 8 covers LED working principle (electroluminescence under forward bias), radiative recombination, wavelength formula lambda = hc/E_g, semiconductor materials (GaAs, GaAsP, GaP), features, advantages, and disadvantages.

coverage.topic: Applications of LED
coverage.evidence: Page 8 lists LED applications including optical fiber communication sources, general illumination, status/message displays, traffic signals, and automotive lighting.

coverage.topic: Super conductivity
coverage.evidence: Page 2 introduces the superconducting state with zero DC electrical resistance and magnetic flux expulsion below a characteristic transition temperature.

coverage.topic: Transition temperature
coverage.evidence: Page 2 defines the transition (critical) temperature T_c below which a material becomes superconducting.

coverage.topic: Critical field
coverage.evidence: Page 2 explains how a magnetic field destroys superconductivity and gives the temperature dependence H_c(T) = H_c(0)[1 - (T/T_c)^2] for T < T_c.

coverage.topic: Meissner effect
coverage.evidence: Page 2 defines the Meissner effect as the expulsion of magnetic flux from the interior of a bulk superconductor (near-perfect diamagnetism) and explains magnetic levitation via persistent screening currents.

coverage.topic: Type I and Type II Super conductors
coverage.evidence: Page 2 compares Type I (single critical field H_c, elemental metals) and Type II (lower and upper critical fields H_c1 and H_c2, vortex mixed state, high-field alloys/compounds) in a table and text.

coverage.topic: Applications of superconductors
coverage.evidence: Page 2 describes applications including MRI and NMR magnets, Maglev systems, SQUIDs, and superconducting power cables and fault-current limiters.

coverage.topic: Dielectric constant
coverage.evidence: Page 3 defines dielectric materials and the dielectric constant epsilon_r = epsilon / epsilon_0 along with its physical properties.

coverage.topic: Polarization
coverage.evidence: Page 4 defines polarization P as the net induced dipole moment per unit volume (C/m^2), polarizability alpha, susceptibility chi, and P = N*mu = N*alpha*E.

coverage.topic: Permittivity - relative permittivity
coverage.evidence: Page 3 defines relative permittivity epsilon_r as the ratio of medium permittivity epsilon to free-space permittivity epsilon_0.

coverage.topic: Relation between polarization and dielectric constant
coverage.evidence: Page 4 relates epsilon_r = 1 + chi via D = epsilon_0 E + P; Page 5 uses Gauss's law for a parallel plate capacitor with and without dielectric to derive D = epsilon_0 E + P and P = E epsilon_0 (epsilon_r - 1).

coverage.topic: Types of Polarization
coverage.evidence: Page 6 explains electronic, ionic, orientation, and space charge polarization, including formulas for alpha_e, alpha_i, and alpha_o, temperature dependence, and total polarization P = P_e + P_i + P_o.

coverage.topic: Internal fields in liquids and solids
coverage.evidence: Page 7 defines the Lorentz internal/local field E_m inside a spherical cavity and evaluates the four components E_1, E_2, E_3, E_4 to derive E_m = E + P / (3 epsilon_0).

coverage.topic: Clausius Mossotti Relation
coverage.evidence: Page 8 provides the full step-by-step derivation of the Clausius-Mossotti equation: (epsilon_r - 1) / (epsilon_r + 2) = N * alpha / (3 * epsilon_0).

coverage.topic: Dielectric loss (qualitative)
coverage.evidence: Page 9 explains dielectric loss in alternating fields due to dipole reversal and gives the power loss formula P = V^2 * omega * C * tan(phi).

coverage.topic: Dielectric breakdown (qualitative)
coverage.evidence: Pages 8 and 9 define dielectric breakdown and explain five breakdown mechanisms: intrinsic, thermal, electrochemical, discharge, and defect breakdown.

coverage.topic: Optical processes - Absorption
coverage.evidence: Page 2 explains induced absorption (A + h*nu = A*) and gives the transition rate B_12 * N_1 * U(nu).

coverage.topic: Optical processes - Spontaneous emission and stimulated emission
coverage.evidence: Page 2 explains spontaneous emission (A* = A + h*nu, rate A_21 * N_2) and stimulated emission (A* + h*nu = A + 2h*nu, rate B_21 * N_2 * U(nu)) and provides a 9-point comparison table.

coverage.topic: Properties of laser
coverage.evidence: Page 2 describes directionality, monochromaticity, coherence, and brightness; Page 5 compares laser light with ordinary light.

coverage.topic: Principle of laser - conditions for sustained lasing
coverage.evidence: Pages 2, 3, and 4 explain that stimulated emission must dominate spontaneous emission, listing the conditions: large radiation density u(nu) via mirror feedback, population inversion (N_2 > N_1), and a metastable upper state (small A_21/B_21).

coverage.topic: Population inversion
coverage.evidence: Page 3 explains thermal equilibrium via Boltzmann's distribution N_2/N_1 = e^{-(E_2 - E_1)/kT} and defines population inversion as the non-equilibrium state N_2 > N_1.

coverage.topic: Pumping
coverage.evidence: Pages 3 and 4 define pumping and describe optical, electrical, chemical, and electron-beam pumping mechanisms.

coverage.topic: Metastable states
coverage.evidence: Page 3 explains why two-level systems fail (10^{-8} s lifetime) and defines metastable states (10^{-3} to 10^{-2} s lifetime) that trap excited atoms to build population inversion.

coverage.topic: Basic components of laser - Active medium
coverage.evidence: Page 4 defines the active medium and active centers (e.g., Cr^{3+} ions in ruby laser, Ne atoms in He-Ne laser).

coverage.topic: Basic components of laser - Optical resonant cavity
coverage.evidence: Page 4 explains the structure and working of the optical resonator (fully reflecting mirror, partially reflecting mirror, and active medium) with a JSXGraph diagram.

coverage.topic: Construction and working of Ruby laser
coverage.evidence: Page 5 details the construction (Al_2O_3:Cr^{3+} rod, helical Xenon flash tube, silvered ends, cooling) and 3-level working (4200 A and 5500 A absorption bands, non-radiative decay to metastable state, 6943 A pulsed laser emission) with an energy level diagram.

coverage.topic: Semiconductor Laser (Qualitative)
coverage.evidence: Page 5 describes the p-n junction diode laser structure (cleaved/polished facets, roughened sides), high forward bias carrier injection, threshold current density I_th, wavelength relation E_g = hc/lambda, advantages, and comparison with LEDs.

coverage.topic: Applications of laser
coverage.evidence: Page 5 covers applications in medical surgery/ophthalmology, microelectronics, industrial drilling/cutting/welding, heat treatment, and pure sciences (physics, chemistry, biology).

coverage.topic: Optical fiber - Principle of propagation of light
coverage.evidence: Page 6 explains Total Internal Reflection (TIR), its two necessary conditions (n_1 > n_2 and i > theta_c), and the core/cladding/buffer structure of an optical fiber.

coverage.topic: Types of fibers - Step index and Graded index fibers
coverage.evidence: Page 6 classifies step-index (single-mode and multimode) and graded-index fibers, plots their normalized refractive index profiles and ray paths, and compares them in an 8-point table; Page 7 adds a single-mode vs multimode comparison table.

coverage.topic: Numerical aperture - Derivation
coverage.evidence: Page 7 defines Numerical Aperture and acceptance angle, derives NA = sin(alpha_m) = sqrt(n_1^2 - n_2^2) using Snell's law at the entry face and critical angle at the core-cladding interface, and includes 3 solved numerical problems.

coverage.topic: Applications of optical fibers
coverage.evidence: Page 7 lists advantages over copper cables and applications in general engineering (defence, space, sensors, NDT, LAN/WAN, cable TV) and medicine (endoscopy, ophthalmology, plaque vaporization, biosensing).

coverage.topic: Fiber optic communication system (block diagram)
coverage.evidence: Page 7 includes the block diagram image and explains all 7 functional units: subscriber telephone, encoder (ADC), optical transmitter (laser/LED), optical fiber link, photodetector, decoder (DAC), and receiving telephone.

Module 2, Page 4: In the table 'Comparison: p-n Junction Diode vs. Zener Diode', item 4 in the p-n Junction Diode column is misnumbered as '5.' resulting in two items numbered '5.' in the right column.
Module 3, Page 1: In 'Your path through this module', the numbered list is out of numerical order: item 1 is followed by item 3, then item 2, then 4.

reader_issues: Two parallel sets of notes are supplied (`chemistry-module-1..4` and `chemistry-ece-module-1..4`). While `chemistry-module-1..4` is complete, rigorous, and 100% aligned with the GXCYT122 syllabus, `chemistry-ece-module-1..4` contains severe gaps and scientific/typographical errors.

In `chemistry-ece-module-4`, the entire final portion of Module 4 (`E Waste, Methods of disposal – recycle, recovery and reuse`, `Chemistry of climate change - Greenhouse Gases`, `Ozone Depletion`, and `Sustainable Development - an introduction to Sustainable Development Goals`) is completely missing.

In `chemistry-ece-module-1` (page 7), the H2-O2 fuel cell is taught using an alkaline electrolyte (25% KOH/NaOH), directly violating the official syllabus specification `H2-O2 fuel cell (acid electrolyte only)`.
In `chemistry-ece-module-1` (page 9), under `Electroless Plating of Copper`, the overall chemical equation is mistakenly written for Nickel plating (`Ni2+ + H2PO2- + H2O -> Ni + H2PO3- + 2H+`).

In `chemistry-ece-module-1` (pages 3 and 5), standard electrode potentials and Celsius temperatures use a bullet symbol (`E^\bullet`, `25^\bullet C`) instead of the degree/standard circle symbol (`E^\circ`, `25^\circ C`), and missing percentage signs occur on page 7 (`charging only up to 90 (x=0.9)`, `40 > Ni-Cd`, `25 KOH`, `efficient (75 )`).
In `chemistry-ece-module-1` (page 5), the glass electrode is misclassified as a secondary/internal reference electrode rather than an ion-selective indicator electrode.

In `chemistry-ece-module-2` (page 7), `Al2O3`, `MgO`, and `SrTiO3` are misclassified as metal-based spintronic materials instead of insulating oxide barriers, and `(Co, Fe, B)` is misclassified as a semiconductor-based spintronic material.
In `chemistry-ece-module-3` (page 7), a stray apostrophe in LaTeX `\(\prime\varepsilon''\)` causes a rendering artifact.
In `chemistry-ece-module-4` (page 5), an unescaped LaTeX command `(\text{HOCl})` appears outside math delimiters.
In `chemistry-ece-module-4` (page 3), the molecular/equivalent weight of `HCO3-` is erroneously tabulated and used as `122` instead of `61`.
uncertainties: Both `chemistry-module-1..4` (assets under `notes/cse/s1/chemistry/...`) and `chemistry-ece-module-1..4` (assets under `notes/ece/s1/chemistry/...`) are supplied for Group B course GXCYT122 (shared between Groups A & B). If Group B students are served `chemistry-ece-module-1..4`, they are missing four major Module 4 topics and face multiple syllabus/chemical errors.

coverage.topic: Defining and using functions in Python

coverage.topic: Functions with multiple return values

coverage.topic: Decomposition and Modularisation Example: Merge sort
coverage.evidence: Page 30 ('Example: decompose merge sort') includes only a 3-sentence conceptual paragraph without decomposing or modularising Merge Sort into Python functions in Module 3 (the full implementation is deferred to Module 4, page 4).
coverage.needed_fix: Include a concrete modular Python decomposition example of Merge Sort (showing `merge_sort` and `merge` functions) or cross-link the full code directly in Module 3.

coverage.topic: Decomposition and Modularisation Example: returning the top three integers from a list of n>=3 integers

coverage.topic: Recursion Defined
coverage.evidence: Page 31 defines a recursive function, base case, and recursive case.

coverage.topic: Reasons for using Recursion
coverage.evidence: Page 30 ('Why use recursion?') explains natural self-similar structure, clarity of correctness arguments, and trade-offs.

coverage.topic: The Call Stack
coverage.evidence: Page 31 ('Call stack and stack frames') explains stack frames, local variables, return addresses, and push/pop order.

coverage.topic: Recursion and the Stack
coverage.evidence: Page 31 traces `factorial(3)` descending and returning across stack frames and notes `RecursionError` when base cases are missed.

coverage.topic: Avoiding Circularity in Recursion
coverage.evidence: Page 31 ('Avoid circularity') explains the three checks to ensure progress toward a base case and avoid circular calls.

coverage.topic: Sample problem (Recursion): Finding the nth Fibonacci number
coverage.evidence: Page 31 provides the recursive `fibonacci(n)` Python function.

coverage.topic: Sample problem (Recursion): greatest common divisor of two positive integers
coverage.evidence: Page 31 provides Euclid's recursive `gcd(a, b)` Python function.

coverage.topic: Sample problem (Recursion): the factorial of a positive integer
coverage.evidence: Page 31 provides the recursive `factorial(n)` Python function and stack trace.

coverage.topic: Sample problem (Recursion): adding two positive integers
coverage.evidence: Page 31 provides the recursive `add(a, b)` Python function.

coverage.topic: Sample problem (Recursion): the sum of digits of a positive number

coverage.topic: Brute-force Approach
coverage.evidence: Page 3 explains the brute-force (exhaustive search) approach, its characteristics, and limitations.

coverage.topic: Brute-force Approach - Example: Padlock
coverage.evidence: Page 3 ('Example: padlock combination') explains the 4-digit padlock search space (10^4), includes a diagram, and provides `crack_lock` Python code.

coverage.topic: Brute-force Approach - Example: Password guessing
coverage.evidence: Page 3 ('Example: password-guessing search space') explains 3-letter password enumeration (26^3 = 17,576) with Python code.

coverage.evidence: Page 4 explains the three steps of Divide and Conquer (Divide, Conquer, Combine), base cases, and includes a diagram.

coverage.topic: Divide-and-conquer Approach - Example: The Merge Sort Algorithm
coverage.evidence: Page 4 ('Example: merge sort') explains the algorithm, provides a split/merge tree diagram on [7, 6, 1, 5, 4, 3], and gives complete Python code.

coverage.topic: Advantages of Divide and Conquer Approach
coverage.evidence: Page 4 ('Advantages') lists 5 advantages: simplifies difficult problems, efficiency, cache usage, numerical accuracy, and parallel execution.

coverage.topic: Disadvantages of Divide and Conquer Approach
coverage.evidence: Page 4 ('Disadvantages') lists 3 disadvantages: recursion overhead, complexity for large inputs, and overkill for simple tasks.

coverage.topic: Dynamic Programming Approach

coverage.topic: Recursion vs Dynamic Programming

coverage.topic: Motivations for the Greedy Approach

coverage.topic: Characteristics of the Greedy Algorithm

coverage.topic: Fuels: Calorific value – HCV and LCV
coverage.evidence: Page 2 and Page 3 define Calorific Value, HCV, LCV, and their mathematical relationship, plus Dulong's formula.

coverage.topic: Experimental determination of calorific value of solid fuels
coverage.evidence: Page 2 and Page 3 cover Bomb Calorimeter construction, working, calculations, and experimental corrections (fuse wire, acid, cooling).

coverage.topic: Analysis of coal – Proximate analysis
coverage.evidence: Page 4 covers classification of coal ranks and Proximate Analysis (moisture, volatile matter, ash, fixed carbon) with procedures, formulas, and significance.

coverage.topic: Octane & Cetane Number
coverage.evidence: Page 4 and Page 5 cover knocking, Cetane number (n-hexadecane and 1-methylnaphthalene), and Octane number (iso-octane and n-heptane).

coverage.topic: Biofuels- Biodiesel
coverage.evidence: Page 5 and Page 6 cover biofuels, biodiesel definition, production via transesterification of rapeseed oil, and advantages.

coverage.topic: Green Hydrogen
coverage.evidence: Page 6 covers hydrogen classification (Blue, Grey, Brown, Pink, Green), electrolytic water splitting, electrolyzers (AWE, PEMWE, SOWE), and applications of green hydrogen.

coverage.topic: Lubricants: Classification - Solid, Semisolid and Liquid lubricants
coverage.evidence: Page 7 covers Semisolid lubricants (Greases: calcium, lithium, sodium, aluminum, axle) and Liquid lubricants (vegetable/animal, mineral, synthetic). Solid lubricants (e.g., graphite, MoS2) are missing from the classification section.
coverage.needed_fix: Add a section explaining Solid Lubricants (such as graphite and molybdenum disulfide, their structure, properties, and applications) under Classification of Lubricants on Page 7.

coverage.topic: Properties of lubricants - Viscosity Index, Flash point, Fire point, Cloud Point, Pour Point & Aniline Point
coverage.evidence: Page 7 covers Viscosity and Viscosity Index (with formula), Flash and Fire Point, Cloud and Pour Point, and Aniline Point.

coverage.topic: Cement: Manufacture of Portland cement
coverage.evidence: Page 8 covers classification of cement, raw materials, dry and wet mixing processes, rotary kiln zones, clinker formation, and mixing with gypsum.

coverage.topic: Theory of setting and hardening of cement
coverage.evidence: Page 8 briefly defines stiffening, setting, and hardening as physical stages and mentions microstructural formation, but omits the specific chemical hydration reactions of C3A, C4AF, C3S, and C2S with water and gypsum.
coverage.needed_fix: Add detailed chemical equations and explanations for the hydration, setting, and hardening reactions of individual clinker compounds (C3A, C3S, C2S, C4AF).

coverage.topic: Nanomaterials: Classification based on Dimension & Materials
coverage.evidence: Page 11 covers Dimensional Classification (0-D, 1-D, 2-D, 3-D) and Classification Based on Materials (carbon-based, metal-based, nanocomposites, dendrimers, biological).

coverage.topic: Synthesis – Sol gel & Chemical Reduction
coverage.evidence: Page 11 covers Sol-Gel Method (with Al(OR)3 hydrolysis equation) and Chemical and Electrochemical Reduction (AgNO3 reduction with trisodium citrate and Cu electro-reduction).

coverage.topic: Applications of nanomaterials
coverage.evidence: Page 11 lists general applications of nanomaterials in solar cells, dense parts/coatings, transistors, paper batteries, and supercapacitors.

coverage.topic: Supercapacitor Materials
coverage.evidence: Pages 11 and 12 briefly mention in bullet points that carbon-based nanoparticles, graphene, and CNTs are used in supercapacitors/ultra-capacitors, but there is no dedicated explanation of supercapacitor materials, principles, or classification.
coverage.needed_fix: Add a dedicated subsection on Supercapacitor Materials explaining what supercapacitors are and the types of nanomaterials used as electrodes (e.g., carbon nanomaterials, metal oxides, conducting polymers).

coverage.topic: Carbon Nanotubes, Fullerenes & Graphene – structure, properties & application
coverage.evidence: Pages 11 and 12 detail the structure, properties, and applications of Graphene, Carbon Nanotubes (SWNTs, MWNTs), and Fullerenes (C60).

coverage.topic: Polymers: ABS & Kevlar - Synthesis, properties and applications
coverage.evidence: Pages 8 and 9 detail the synthesis reactions, bonding, properties, and uses of ABS and Kevlar.

coverage.topic: Conducting Polymers- Classification – Application
coverage.evidence: Pages 9 and 10 cover the classification (intrinsically conducting, p-doping, n-doping, extrinsically conducting) and conduction mechanisms thoroughly, but applications of conducting polymers are missing.
coverage.needed_fix: Add a section listing the engineering applications of conducting polymers (e.g., OLEDs, sensors, rechargeable batteries, antistatic coatings, smart windows).

coverage.topic: Electrochemical Cell
coverage.evidence: Page 2 covers Electrolytic vs. Galvanic cells, Daniell cell reactions, IUPAC cell representation, and salt bridge functions.

coverage.topic: Electrode potential
coverage.evidence: Pages 2, 3, and 4 discuss types of electrodes, measurement of electrode potential using SCE, and standard reduction/oxidation potentials in the electrochemical series, but lack a formal definition and explanation of the origin of single electrode potential (Helmholtz electrical double layer) and standard electrode potential.
coverage.needed_fix: Add explicit definitions and theoretical explanation for the origin of electrode potential and standard electrode potential on Page 2.

coverage.topic: Nernst equation for single electrode and cell (Numerical problems)
coverage.evidence: Nernst equation is only briefly mentioned in specific contexts: for Glass electrode on Page 3 (Eg = Eg0 - 0.0591 pH) and equilibrium constant on Page 4 (E = E0 - (0.0591/n) log K). The general Nernst equation derivation/formulation for a single electrode and complete cell, as well as worked numerical problems, are missing.
coverage.needed_fix: Add the derivation and general expressions of the Nernst equation for single electrodes and complete electrochemical cells, along with solved numerical problems.

coverage.topic: Reference electrodes – SHE & Calomel electrode – Construction and Working
coverage.evidence: Pages 3 and 4 cover SHE (construction, characteristics, reactions, drawbacks) and Saturated Calomel Electrode (construction, electrode reaction, working for potential measurement, advantages).

coverage.topic: Electrochemical series - Applications
coverage.evidence: Page 4 defines the electrochemical series and explains its applications (relative ease of oxidation/reduction, acid reaction to give H2, standard EMF calculation, displacement reactions, equilibrium constant, feasibility of redox reactions).

coverage.topic: Glass Electrode & pH Measurement
coverage.evidence: Page 3 covers glass electrode construction, ion exchange mechanism, Nernst equation for glass electrode, and determination of unknown pH by coupling with SCE.

coverage.topic: Conductivity- Measurement using Digital conductivity meter
coverage.evidence: Page 5 covers Ohm's law, resistance, conductance, resistivity, specific conductance (conductivity), cell constant determination with 0.1 M KCl, and conductivity measurement using a digital conductivity meter.

coverage.topic: Li-ion battery & H2-O2 fuel cell (acid electrolyte only) construction and working

coverage.topic: Linear systems of equations: Gauss elimination
coverage.evidence: Pages 2, 3, 7, and 8 explain matrix representations Ax = b, augmented matrices, elementary row operations, Gaussian elimination to upper triangular form, and back substitution with multiple worked examples.

coverage.topic: Row echelon form
coverage.evidence: Pages 4 and 9 define row echelon form (pivots stepping strictly to the right, zero rows at the bottom) and apply echelon reduction to multiple matrices.

coverage.topic: Linear Independence: rank of a matrix
coverage.evidence: Pages 4 and 9 define linear combinations, linear independence/dependence of vectors, and matrix rank as the number of pivots in row echelon form (with rank(A) = rank(A^T)), alongside worked problems for 3x3, 3x4, and 4x4 matrices.

coverage.topic: Solutions of linear systems: Existence, Uniqueness (without proof)
coverage.evidence: Pages 4, 8, and 9 state and apply the Fundamental Theorem for Linear Systems: consistency iff rank(A) = rank([A|b]), unique solution when r = n, and infinitely many solutions with n - r free variables when r < n.

coverage.topic: The matrix Eigen Value Problem
coverage.evidence: Pages 5 and 10 formulate Ax = \lambda x, (A - \lambda I)x = 0, the characteristic equation det(A - \lambda I) = 0, spectrum, spectral radius, and trace/minor invariant formulas.

coverage.topic: Determining Eigen values and Eigen vector
coverage.evidence: Pages 5, 10, and 11 provide detailed worked examples computing eigenvalues and eigenvectors for 2x2 and 3x3 matrices, including distinct, repeated, defective, and complex conjugate eigenvalues.

coverage.topic: Diagonalization of matrices
coverage.evidence: Pages 6 and 12 explain eigenspaces, algebraic and geometric multiplicity, modal matrix X, similarity transformation D = X^(-1)AX, matrix powers, and worked 2x2 and 3x3 diagonalization examples.

coverage.topic: Homogeneous linear ODEs of second order
coverage.evidence: Pages 2 and 6 introduce standard form y'' + p(x)y' + q(x)y = 0, solution verification, linear independence, Wronskian, and reduction of order.

coverage.topic: Superposition principle
coverage.evidence: Page 2 explicitly explains the superposition principle for homogeneous linear equations: any linear combination y = c_1 y_1 + c_2 y_2 of solutions is also a solution.

coverage.topic: General solution (homogeneous second-order linear ODE)
coverage.evidence: Pages 2 and 6 define a basis (fundamental system) of two linearly independent solutions and form the general solution y = c_1 y_1 + c_2 y_2.

coverage.topic: Homogeneous linear ODEs of second order with constant coefficients (Method to find general solution, solution of linear Initial Value Problem)
coverage.evidence: Pages 3 and 7 derive the characteristic equation \lambda^2 + a\lambda + b = 0, cover all three root cases (distinct real, repeated real, complex conjugate), and solve multiple IVPs.

coverage.topic: Non homogenous ODEs (with constant coefficients) - General solution
coverage.evidence: Pages 4 and 8 explain the structure of the general solution y(x) = y_h(x) + y_p(x) for driven constant-coefficient ODEs.

coverage.topic: Particular solution by the method of undetermined coefficients (Particular solutions for the functions ke^(\gamma x), kx^n, k\cos(\omega x), k\sin(\omega x), ke^(\alpha x)\cos(\omega x), ke^(\alpha x)\sin(\omega x))
coverage.evidence: Pages 4, 8, and 9 state the basic, modification (resonance), and sum rules, present the complete trial-form table for all six listed function families, and work through examples for each.

coverage.topic: Initial value Problem for Non-Homogeneous Second order linear ODE (with constant coefficients)
coverage.evidence: Page 8 works three full non-homogeneous IVPs, emphasizing that initial conditions must be applied to the complete solution y = y_h + y_p.

coverage.topic: Solution by variation of parameters (Second Order)
coverage.evidence: Pages 5 and 10 derive and apply the Wronskian-based variation of parameters formula across five worked problems.

coverage.topic: Laplace Transform
coverage.evidence: Pages 2 and 7 define the unilateral Laplace transform integral and derive/apply transforms for standard elementary and trigonometric functions.

coverage.topic: Inverse Laplace Transform
coverage.evidence: Pages 3, 8, and 9 cover inverse Laplace transforms via table lookup, completing the square, and partial fraction decomposition.

coverage.topic: Linearity property
coverage.evidence: Pages 2, 3, 7, and 8 state and apply the linearity property for both forward and inverse Laplace transforms.

coverage.topic: First shifting theorem
coverage.evidence: Pages 3, 7, and 8 explain and apply L{e^(at)f(t)} = F(s - a) in both forward and inverse directions.

coverage.topic: Transform of derivatives
coverage.evidence: Pages 4 and 10 state and explain the Laplace transform formulas for first and second derivatives: L{y'} = sY(s) - y(0) and L{y''} = s^2Y(s) - sy(0) - y'(0).

coverage.topic: Solution of Initial value problems by Laplace transform (Second order linear ODE with constant coefficients with initial conditions at t=0 only)
coverage.evidence: Pages 4 and 10 demonstrate the full pipeline for solving second-order constant-coefficient IVPs with initial conditions at t = 0.

coverage.topic: Unit step function
coverage.evidence: Pages 6 and 12 define the Heaviside unit step function u(t - a) and its Laplace transform e^(-as)/s.

coverage.topic: Second shifting theorem
coverage.evidence: Pages 6 and 12 state L{f(t - a)u(t - a)} = e^(-as)F(s) and demonstrate algebraic time-shifting in worked examples.

coverage.topic: Dirac delta function and its transform (Initial value problems involving unit step function and Dirac delta function are excluded)
coverage.evidence: Pages 6 and 12 define the Dirac delta impulse \delta(t - a), its sifting property, and its transform L{f(t)\delta(t - a)} = f(a)e^(-as) and L{\delta(t - a)} = e^(-as), while appropriately excluding IVPs with step/delta inputs.

coverage.topic: Convolution theorem (without proof) and its application to finding inverse Laplace transform of products of functions
coverage.evidence: Pages 5 and 11 define the convolution integral (f * g)(t), state the Convolution Theorem, and work through six inverse transform problems of products F(s)G(s).

coverage.topic: Taylor series representation (without proof, assuming the possibility of power series expansion in appropriate domains)
coverage.evidence: Pages 2 and 6 state the Taylor series formula centered at x_0 and work multiple examples (ln x, 1/x, 1/(1+x) at x_0 = 1) along with regions of convergence.

coverage.topic: Maclaurin series representation
coverage.evidence: Pages 2 and 6 state the Maclaurin formula (x_0 = 0), provide standard expansions for e^x, sin x, cos x, and 1/(1-x), and derive several series via derivatives and algebraic substitution.

coverage.topic: Fourier series
coverage.evidence: Pages 3, 7, and 8 define periodic functions, fundamental period 2L, and the trigonometric Fourier series representation.

coverage.topic: Euler formulas
coverage.evidence: Pages 3, 7, and 8 state and apply Euler's integral formulas for Fourier coefficients a_0, a_n, and b_n.

coverage.topic: Convergence of Fourier series (Dirichlet's conditions)
coverage.evidence: Pages 3 and 4 state Dirichlet's conditions and Dirichlet's convergence theorem (converging to f(x_0) at continuity points and [f(x_0^-) + f(x_0^+)]/2 at jump discontinuities), applying it throughout pages 4, 7, 8, 9, and 10.

coverage.topic: Fourier series of 2\pi periodic functions
coverage.evidence: Pages 4 and 7 work through seven full Fourier series problems on (-\pi, \pi) and [0, 2\pi].

coverage.topic: Fourier series of 2l periodic functions
coverage.evidence: Pages 3 and 8 formulate and solve six Fourier series problems on arbitrary intervals [-L, L] and [0, 2L].

coverage.topic: Half range sine series expansion
coverage.evidence: Pages 5 and 10 explain odd periodic extensions on [0, L] and work five half-range sine series problems.

coverage.topic: Half range cosine series expansion
coverage.evidence: Pages 5 and 9 explain even periodic extensions on [0, L] and work five half-range cosine series problems.

reader_issues: Inconsistent notation for the Fourier constant term in Module 4: Page 3 and Page 5 use a_0/2 with a_0 = (1/L)\int f(x)dx (and 2/L for half-range), whereas Pages 7, 8, and 9 write the series with bare a_0 and define a_0 = (1/2L)\int f(x)dx (and 1/L for half-range) without alerting the reader to the convention switch.

Several worked problems preserve transcription/source errors in their final Answer lines (even when a 'Watch out' box notes the error): e.g., Module 1 Page 11 Problem Q (matrix entries switched in solution); Module 2 Page 7 Problem 4.3 (extra '3 +' in final answer), Page 9 Problem 8 (wrong root e^(-3x) and sign +1/4 in answer), Page 9 Problem 4 (wrong root e^(-2x) in answer); Module 3 Page 7 Problems 10, 11, 16 (typos in final answers), Page 8 Problem 8 (unshifted numerator and wrong exponent in answer), Page 10 Problem 2 (dropped 's' in numerator) and Problem 4 (t^3 instead of t^2 in answer), Page 11 Problems 4 and 5 (typos in final answers); Module 4 Page 8 Problem 4.2.12 (upper limit evaluated at 1 instead of 2) and Problem 4.2.8 (typos in final series).

Image references in Module 1 (page 7, 9) and Module 4 (pages 7, 8, 9, 10) point to '/assets/notes/ece/s1/maths/...' SVGs whose visual rendering cannot be verified from markdown text alone, though surrounding equations substantively cover the concepts.

reader_issues: In python-module-1 (pages 1 through 12), almost every page contains duplicated content: the second half of each page repeats the exact same concepts, examples, and code from the first half of that page.
In python-module-1 (page 4), the repeated Class Average formula writes `Average (in percentage) = (Average_2 / 13)` instead of `(Average_2 / 12) * 100`.
In python-module-1 (page 4), the binary machine code formula is mangled in the second repetition (`1010 0011_{add} 0110_{3} _{6}`).

In python-module-1 (page 7), the explicit type conversion code snippet has misaligned comments (`y = int(x); print(y + 5)` followed by `# Output: 15`, and `z = float(y)` where `y` is 15 followed by `# Output: 10.0`).

In python-module-1 (page 10), the Assignment Operators output says `a += 5 : 105` when `a` was initialized to `10` (should be `15`, and subsequent values `10`, `50`, `10.0` are also off by a factor of 10).
In python-module-1 (page 11), the Bitwise Operators output prints `a >> 2 : 240` instead of `a << 2 : 240` for the left-shift label, and a stray word `College` appears by itself after Example 5.4.
In python-module-1 (page 12), C-style logical operators (`C&&D`, `||`) are used in the expression evaluation table for a Python expression using `and` and `or`.
In python-module-1 (page 13), Expression 2 evaluation has a typo: `not False evaluates to (False)` instead of `True`.
In python-module-2, HTML page comments alternate `<!-- page 26 -->` and `<!-- page 27 -->` repeatedly for source pages 15 through 30.
uncertainties: Several flowchart and diagram images in Modules 1, 2, 3, and 4 are external `.webp` assets; their internal visual details are inferred from surrounding text and alt attributes.
